articles.title: Elf Is A Holiday Classic Now, But One Star Admits It Was ‘Risky’ Business At The Time
articles.summary: It's hard to imagine Christmas without Buddy the Elf, but Hollywood wasn't convinced the movie would work.
articles.content:
With the holiday season upon us and the 2026 movie calendar winding down, there are a handful of the best Christmas movies I return to every December, and Elf is pretty much guaranteed to make the list. Will Ferrell running around New York City in yellow tights, eating spaghetti covered in candy and screaming about Santa Claus has become as much a part of the holidays as putting up the tree. According to one of the movie's stars, Hollywood wasn't exactly convinced it had a future Christmas classic on its hands back in 2003.

Considering Will Ferrell himself had doubts when he first tried on Buddy's iconic costume, I can understand why some studio executives might have been nervous. At the time, the SNL alum was best known for his work on Saturday Night Live , where he'd spent seven seasons establishing himself as one of the show's biggest stars. He'd appeared in movies like Old School and Zoolander , but he hadn't yet proven he could carry a major studio comedy as its leading man.

It's funny to think about now, considering Ferrell went on to become one of the biggest comedy stars of the 2000s, while Favreau would eventually direct Iron Man , helping launch the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He's also had a major hand in shaping the modern Star Wars franchise with The Mandalorian . But back in 2003, the idea of giving a relatively untested leading man a Christmas comedy about a grown man raised by elves probably sounded pretty ridiculous on paper. And considering some of the behind-the-scenes stories about making Elf , it's remarkable how well everything came together. It is a ridiculous premise. That's a big part of why I love it.

Richter also credited the combination of Ferrell's comedic instincts and Favreau's approach to storytelling for making the movie work. Interestingly, though, the movie’s star recently addressed the longstanding rumors about his relationship with Favreau during the production. It seems there's still plenty to learn about what went into making this particular Christmas classic. As for Richter, he told the outlet that the film succeeds because:

I think that's a pretty accurate assessment. Ferrell gets to be completely absurd as Buddy, whether he's congratulating a coffee shop for having the world's best cup of coffee or trying to navigate a revolving door. Yet the movie also gives us a genuinely sweet story about a guy looking for his father and trying to find somewhere he belongs.

More than two decades later, it's difficult to imagine the holiday season without Buddy the Elf. The movie remains a favorite among families, and people are still finding new things to appreciate about it, including one particularly interesting question about Buddy's journey from the North Pole to New York City.

articles.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home Already Revealed the Perfect Way for Marvel to Bring Back This Legacy Character
articles.summary: The multiversal adventures of Spider-Man: No Way Home were a lot more than just the chance to bring Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield into the MCU. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The multiversal adventures of Spider-Man: No Way Home were a lot more than just the chance to bring Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield into the MCU. The film proved that perhaps nothing was off-limits for the Multiverse Saga . Any Marvel hero or villain who had appeared onscreen, be it on TV or film, could potentially make a surprise return within the MCU, given if the story could justify their travel from one universe to the next. And it’s a narrative device Marvel has used time and again in the lead-up to Avengers: Doomsday , continually expanding the limits of what fans thought was possible.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and Deadpool & Wolverine both dealt extensively with the revival of characters from other studios’ Marvel productions. Suddenly, Patrick Stewart’s Professor X was interacting with Benedict Cumberbatch’s Doctor Strange, and Jennifer Garner’s Elektra and Wesley Snipes’ Blade joined Ryan Reynolds’ Deadpool and Hugh Jackman’s Wolverine in battle. Although Marvel has established a number of clever ways to circle back to characters from past projects, Spider-Man: No Way Home revealed the precise strategy the MCU can still use to bring back one of its few remaining forgotten big-screen heroes one last time.

Between 1998 and 2007, 16 theatrical films were based on Marvel Comics properties. This includes Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man trilogy, the Blade trilogy, the original X-Men trilogy, two Fantastic Four films, Ang Lee’s Hulk , The Punisher starring Thomas Jane, Daredevil , and its spinoff Elektra . But just a year before the MCU launched with Iron Man , Oscar winner Nicolas Cage starred in the big-screen version of Ghost Rider . The film received poor reviews but managed to earn nearly $230 million at the worldwide box office against a production budget of at least $110 million. So a sequel, Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance , was released in 2012, earning a modest profit too but also disappointing fans overall.

Aside from appearances on Agents of SHIELD , Ghost Rider has been largely absent from Marvel projects ever since. However, that is about to change with Ryan Gosling set to play Johnny Blaze in the upcoming Ghost Rider film. As one of the first MCU films coming after Avengers: Secret Wars , Gosling’s adventure will almost certainly be set in the rumored consolidated version of the Sacred Timeline following the collapse of the multiverse. If that’s the case, then time is running out for Cage to reprise the role and grandfather his pair of films into the MCU tapestry like so many other legacy properties.

Cage has previously expressed a lack of interest in joining the MCU. After all, he is coming off of recently playing another Marvel character, the title hero on Amazon Prime Video’s Spider-Noir series. And he's expected to reprise that role again in next year’s Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse . And the last time he made a cameo appearance in a multiversal superhero extravaganza was the 2023 DC film The Flash , in which he played a version of Superman he nearly played in the 1990s. Thankfully, unlike that confusing experience , there’s no need for Cage to even report to set for his Ghost Rider to return in an MCU film.

Spider-Man: No Way Home already employed the perfect, low-stakes way for Cage’s Ghost Rider to ride onto the big screen one more time. That movie used a combination of CGI and archive footage to bring the Spidey villains The Lizard and Sandman back to the franchise. Actors Rhys Ifans and Thomas Haden Church , respectively, only had to lend their voices to the project. As such, Cage could simply record his lines to return as Ghost Rider. After all, the character is best known as a motorcyclist whose visage is defined by its flaming skull. So it wouldn’t be a stretch to have him back without even having to show Cage’s face. It would also finally bring one of the best-known pre-MCU Marvel movie characters into the franchise at last.

Should Marvel use the same movie magic from Spider-Man: No Way Home to bring Nicolas Cage’s Ghost Rider into the MCU? Sound off with your thoughts in the comments section below!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

Gerald R. Molen , an Academy Award-winning producer behind Steven Spielberg 's Amblin Entertainment, has died. He was 91.

"Uncle Jerry was a man of great moral character and high integrity. He started doing work, moving set pieces and driving at a movie studio, and worked his way up to the position of producer. He worked on many great films, including Jurassic Park , Schindler's List (for which he won the Oscar for best production), Rain Man , Minority Report and The Other Side of Heaven , just to name a few. He held to his beliefs and standards and industry where that was often difficult to do. Minority Report is rated PG-13 because Jerry told Steven Spielberg he would only do the movie if it wasn't rated R, and Spielberg made it happen—it was worth it to him to have Jerry be his producer. articles.title: This Classic Spider-Man Villain Recently Made His Live Action Debut, But His First Appearance Comic Released Over 60 Years Ago
articles.summary: Besides the Green Goblin, most of Spider-Man's rogues gallery is filled with dudes with animal powers or suits, like Rhino, Vulture, Doc Ock, The Lizard. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Besides the Green Goblin, most of Spider-Man 's rogues gallery is filled with dudes with animal powers or suits, like Rhino, Vulture, Doc Ock, The Lizard. I suppose a goblin is a mythical animal in its own way too. Call it lazy or creative, the formula perfectly fits into the web of the Spider-Man universe. While we've seen all these villains make their live action appearances in the Marvel Cinematic Universe or Sony's movies, it took Scorpion almost 61 years to make his first live action appearance. With his long awaited debut finally taking place in this year's Spider-Man: Brand New Day , his first appearance comic, The Amazing Spider-Man #20 , was recently sold for $2,379 at Heritage Auctions.

While we don't really get into Scorpion's origins in the movie, you'll actually be pretty surprised to learn how he got his powers in the comic. It turns out J. Jonah Jameson's obsession with Spider-Man was straight up evil in the '60s, with the Daily Bugle boss wanting to kill him. So, upon hearing that there's a scientist dabbling in animal mutations, J.J. takes private investigator Mac Gargan to him in order to get superpowers and the trademark green suit with the tail to defeat Spidey. However, much like all of J.J.'s evil plans, this one also backfires, resulting in the newly superpowered Scorpion going on a criminal rampage. However, as his luck would have it, the editor-in-chief comes off as a hero when he manages to trap Scorpion after Spidey did all the hard work of softening him up.

Now I know what you're thinking; we technically saw Scorpion in Spider-Man: Homecoming , but he didn't have his trademark suit. So, I think it's safe to say that while we saw Mac Gargan in the movie, he only appeared as Scorpion in Brand New Day . It seems Scorpion has suddenly become very popular in the extended Spider-Man universe, as he was also one of the prime antagonists in 2025's Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man animated series. While the feud would continue over the decades, it's strange to think that it was J.J.'s twisted obsession with Spider-Man that gave rise to one of the hero and the city's biggest villains. Modern day J.J. seems like an angel in comparison.

With Scorpion finally making his live action first appearance, we've finally seen all of Spidey's big-ticket baddies; and yes, Paul Giamatti's small appearance as Rhino in The Amazing Spider-Man 2 counts because it was awesome. As for why it took 61 years for it to finally happen, it's probably a mix of Spidey having too many big villains and the whole Sony - Disney rights issue that went on for so many years. Regardless, the next time you see Scorpion in any of his adaptations, just remember that he got his powers and suit almost 61 years ago, all thanks to J. Jonah Jameson's hate for Spider-Man. While the original backstory has been retconned over the years, it's still interesting to see just how despicable the character originally was.

Do you think the wait for Scorpion's live action appearance was worth it? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Everyone Forgets About Spider-Man’s Original Superhero Roommate, but He Helped Debut an Iconic X-Men Villain
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Ever since he swung onto the scene with an origin story that made him an instant classic, Spider-Man has been Marvel's most popular hero. Peter captured a generation of fans with his youthful perspective and problems that, even if people didn't experience them themselves, felt relatable. Spider-Man proceeded to instantly capture an audience that no […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Ever since he swung onto the scene with an origin story that made him an instant classic, Spider-Man has been Marvel's most popular hero. Peter captured a generation of fans with his youthful perspective and problems that, even if people didn't experience them themselves, felt relatable. Spider-Man proceeded to instantly capture an audience that no other hero could compete with , and Marvel has been sure to make use of that in every way that they could over the decades he's been around. After all, Spider-Man regularly trades places with Batman for being the most popular superhero of all time, and that is nowhere near an easy feat.

Case in point, Marvel has never been hesitant to use Spider-Man as a testing ground for some of their lesser-known heroes. Given that he was one of the company's biggest names, even back in the '60s and '70s, a ton of Marvel heroes got their chance to reach a wider audience by working with the Wall-Crawler. One of the greatest examples of this came about in Marvel Team-Up (1972) #65, which not only saw Captain Britain's first adventures in the USA, but also the introduction of the now-iconic X-Men villain, Arcade .

Spider-Man met Captain Britain first in civilian clothes, when college-student Peter Parker found out that he was forced to board the visiting British student Brian Braddock. Peter wasn't thrilled with this arrangement, but he couldn't turn down extra cash, either, even if he was concerned that Brian might figure out his secret identity. Brian nearly did that very night, when he was Spidey swinging out of Peter's window. Not knowing any of the heroes in town, Captain Britain assumed Spidey to be a criminal and attacked. We had a classic superhero-first-meeting fight, but after they cleared things up and made friends, they were both kidnapped by Arcade, who was hired to assassinate the good Captain.

The entirety of the Marvel Team-Up series was based around Spider-Man teaming up with various other heroes to give them a chance to shine, but no other issue succinctly captures this style like this one does. Captain Britain was still a relatively new and niche hero at the time, so throwing him in as Peter's temporary roommate made for a perfect way to force fans to pay attention to him. It even includes a recap of Brian's origins and some of his adventures up to that point, which makes it the perfect issue to get into the character and dive into his comics from there.

Of course, the series was famous for doing the same for villains, too, and it gave us the infamous game-master Arcade himself. Arcade is another niche character, but he's more than carved out his place in Marvel as the master of death traps. Nobody can build a death machine like this lad here, and he takes great pride in that accomplishment. He wouldn't really make a name for himself until he battled the X-Men not too long after, but this issue set the stage with everything the audience needs to know about the mad mechanist. This issue gave us one character's growth and the introduction of another, which really just goes to show how much faith Marvel placed in Spider-Man.

Sure, Captain Britain was already an established hero at the time of this issue's debut, but from the name alone, "Introducing, Captain Britain," it was made to be a first step into the character, and that remains true for so many other iconic characters who hang around Spidey. Black Widow's iconic costume even first appeared in Amazing Spider-Man (1963) #86, for just one example. Punisher blasted onto the scene in Amazing Spider-Man #129. Cloak and Dagger debuted in Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #64. Spider-Man has always been Marvel's number one way to get readers' eyes on the characters that they believed in, but needed capital to make work.

Spider-Man is a hero in many more ways than one. In-universe, he stands as a shining example of how to save the day, and out-of-universe he's a spectacular star that Marvel can attach their lesser-known properties to in order to get them to gather a following. It's an important, necessary job when dealing with so many characters in a shared universe. Superman and Batman have done this duty for nearly their entire existence, and Spider-Man is no different. These heroes draw eyes, and their continued popularity and importance break the ground for others to build their own new ideas on, which is what keeps the blood flowing through these comic books. Being number one is a big ask , but Spider-Man is more than bearing the power responsibly.

Which of Spider-Man's many important introductions is your favorite? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Doomsday Stars Breakdown Gambit & Shang-Chi's Big Fight, And Why It Works
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel There are a lot of big moments in the Avengers: Doomsday trailer that have fans excited for the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe movie. Some of the most exciting scenes showed the battle between members of the Avengers teams and the X-Men. One of the biggest fights seems to be between two team leaders, with Sam […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are a lot of big moments in the Avengers: Doomsday trailer that have fans excited for the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe movie. Some of the most exciting scenes showed the battle between members of the Avengers teams and the X-Men. One of the biggest fights seems to be between two team leaders, with Sam Wilson's Captain America fighting Cyclops of the X-Men . There was also a fight in an earlier trailer between Yelena Belova and Mystique. While both of those fights sound exciting, the best fight of them all might come between Shang-Chi, of Sam Wilson's Avengers team, and Gambit, who is fighting with the X-Men.

This fight will be more than just two superheroes throwing around their powers against each other. Channing Tatum, who returns as Gambit, told Entertainment Weekly that the fight choreography would be like they would "get to be in a kung-fu movie. This is so fun. Anything is possible, literally." Simu Liu, who plays Shang-Chi, added, "To have a scene partner like Channing, who was as insistent as I was about getting to do as much of it as possible, was really critical to the success of that scene."

What Fans Can Expect From Shang-Chi vs. Gambit in Avengers: Doomsday Image Courtesy of Marvel Anyone who remembers how great Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings was should remember what the fight scenes in that movie looked like. While Avengers: Doomsday obviously has different directors, there is no way that Marvel changes how Shang-Chi fights, which involves using the Ten Rings, but also by implementing a strong mix of kung-fu fighting techniques, which is what Channing Tatum was hinting at. While Tatum is not known for this kind of fight choreography, he is a dancer, so it shouldn't have been too hard for him to master the choreography needed to keep up with Simu Liu in these fight scenes.

Of course, there will also be their power sets, with Shang-Chi throwing around his Ten Rings while Gambit tosses his explosive cards in the fight, so it will be more than just kung-fu fighting. However, the only way to make their weapons make sense will be for them to pull off the kung-fu fight scenes, and considering the last Shang-Chi movie and Tatum's incredible dancing skills, this should be one of the best-choreographed and best-executed battles in the new movie.

This won't be the only fight between the X-Men and Avengers, and as mentioned, most eyes will be on Cyclops and Sam Wilson's Captain America. However, don't forget about the Shang-Chi and Gambit fight, which might be the fight that steals the entire movie. As Joe Russo said, the mutants are in a constant fight for their survival, so Gambit is likely to be putting as much into this battle as Shang-Chi.

articles.title: Olivia Colman’s Carrying Around A Wicker Penis (And I Wonder If Alexander Skarsgård Knows)
articles.summary: Didn't have that on my 2026 bingo card. At all.
articles.content:
The Wicker cast has been feeding into innuendo pretty much since all the horny reviews dropped for the 2026 movie release . Having seen the movie in theaters myself, I have to say I wholeheartedly approve. So, I guess I shouldn’t have been surprised when lead Olivia Colman pulled a wicker, penis-shaped vibrator out of her purse during a recent appearance, but I was! I wonder if Alexander Skarsgård knows she has this homage to his member on her person at any given time?

She said fans might be “surprised” she’s just carrying around the wicker contraption, and joked she's “going to say it’s a lipstick" before also pulling out some Kitkats and Twix bars. See the surprise moment, below.

I certainly didn’t see the wicker vibrator coming, but I do have questions. Namely, that doesn’t look like the very uncomfortable prosthetics Alexander Skarsgård was wearing on set. So, like where does one get a wicker vibrator? Did a fan make that and give it to her? Does she keep that in her bag all the time, or was this just tossed in to throw Wicker into the conversation? Again, does her co-star know she's carrying this around?

With a Wicker Oscars push, anything is possible. Honestly I'd be down for some Best Actor/Actress noms. Colman and Skarsgård are so good in the movie and when I saw it in a theater full of women , the crowd was rowdy and having fun with the premise, which was so cheeky and unexpected. Even the merch for this movie follows suit! I mean, the popcorn bucket needs its own intimacy coordinator !

Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki, two of Indian cinema's most celebrated playback singers, were remembered at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa by singer K.S. Chithra and actor-filmmaker Suhasini Maniratnam .

Bhosle, a two-time Grammy nominee whose name was referenced in Cornershop's 1997 hit "Brimful of Asha," died in April at 92 . Janaki, known as the Nightingale of South India, died in July at 88. Chithra, who has recorded more than 25,000 songs in several Indian languages over a career spanning nearly five decades, spoke about the singers who shaped her musical sensibilities, among them Mangeshkar, P. Susheela and Janaki. She imitated Janaki as a child, while acknowledging that the veteran singer's distinctive style was impossible to reproduce. Mangeshkar's devotional songs, she said, had particularly impressed her with their emotional depth.

Rahman, an Oscar winner for "Slumdog Millionaire," had invited Bhosle to record a song that needed to evoke the style of Tamil playback singer L.R. Eswari, but was unsure how to explain the reference to her. He asked Suhasini to help. She demonstrated Eswari's style, and Bhosle went on to deliver "Venilla Venilla."

Chithra spoke about Bhosle's versatility and her ability to move between musical forms, including ghazals, and about her desire to establish her own musical identity rather than be compared with her sister. Janaki, Suhasini said, could inhabit a character through her voice, singing like a child or a teenage boy. Chithra recalled that Janaki was a devoted fan of Mangeshkar. articles.title: 5 Rebel and New Republic Starfighters That Will Blast Through Whatever the Bad Guys Throws at Them

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars made a huge splash when it premiered in 1977, entrancing a whole generation. There are numerous reasons for this – interesting characters, a familiar yet also strangely fresh setting, and "lived-in" feel that made it different from other sci-fi. It was this tech that played a big role in the popularity, especially the ships and vehicles of the Rebel Alliance. Now, there was a pragmatic reason why all of these designs were so cool – Lucas kept the merchandising rights and nothing else at first, so he made sure that there were a lot of toys to sell, making enough money to buy back the rest of the rights to his work – with the wizards of Industrial Light and Magic making some of the coolest sci-fi designs ever.

While the Empire was defined by their massive warships and clouds of TIE Fighters, the Rebels had a more DIY, small scale aesthetic, with their more powerful, better designed fighters allowing them to even up the odds. When the Alliance finally won, the New Republic would take their place in both canon and Star Wars Legends , introducing numerous new fighter designs to defend the galaxy. These 5 Rebel/New Republic fighters, from both canon and Legends, are the best of the best, bringing their pilots home against the worst odds.

Star Wars has some of the most lethal fighters in sci-fi, but there's one that doesn't get nearly enough respect. In fact, it has often got the exact opposite of respect from most, partly because it looks like a wreck (I remember when Luke said in Star Wars: Rogue Squadron for N64 that it handles like a sleepy Hutt). The Y-Wing has a terrible reputation with fans who have only watched the movies, but for those who have moved beyond them, the Y-Wing is one of the most devastating fighters in the galaxy. The ship may look like it's held together with baling wire and tape, but it's actually one of the most durable fighters out there.

Y-Wings were able to take a beating and then be easily rebuilt. Clone Wars surplus, the Rebels stripped the armor off of them, allowing them to work on them easier. Y-Wings were the early backbone of the Alliance, helping the various Rebel cells get some early victories. Armed with two forward laser cannon, a combination missile/torpedo/bomb launching suite (basically, they could modified to use any of those), and an ion cannon turret, it could do a lot of damage and take a lot thanks to its shields. They might have been slow and a bit sluggish on the turns, but they had it where it counted and brought many pilots home that would have died piloting a faster fighter like the A-Wing.

I was a huge fan of the Legends novels that ran from 1991 to 2012. I read nearly all of the ones published by Bantam in the '90s, including Star Wars: The Black Fleet Crisis . This trilogy was about an alien race named the Yevetha. Based in the Deep Core of the galaxy, the Empire enslaved them and forced them to create the Black Fleet. However, at some point after Endor, the Imperials on N'Zoth vanished and xenophobic Yevetha rearmed, ready to paint the Core Worlds with the blood of every species that wasn't them. That's a pretty cool premise, right? I'd love to tell you that it was a good series, but the second book slammed on the breaks, slowing everything to crawl, and the trilogy never recovered (the second book kicked off with Lando, Lobot, and the droids searching a giant empty ship for. A. Hundred. Pages).

However, the first book introduced readers to some of the coolest Star Wars ships of them all, including a new fighter that was a cousin to the Y-Wing. The K-Wing was also made by Koensayr, who wanted to create a fighter that would take everything great about the Y-Wing and enhance it, while also making the fighter generally better. The K-Wing was a heavy bomber; much like the B-Wing, it was made to hit mid-sized warships on its own, and larger ones as squadrons. It was the definition of heavily armed, with a medium-range twin laser cannon turret, a short-range quad-turbolaser battery (that's right, like the big ships) and 18 hardpoints, which could mount weapons concussion missiles, proton torpedoes, plasma torpedo, flechette launchers, homing missiles, ion bombs, and Conner Nets (nets that had ion cannon technology that disabled ships). It was also heavy and slow, although it was fast enough for its size and weight class, with the kinds of weapons, shields, and armor that made up for it. A good K-Wing crew could survive anything.

The E-Wing was introduced in 1991's Star Wars: Dark Empire comics. It was built by Freitek, a company made up of the Incom designers of the X-Wing, for the New Republic. It was meant to be the next generation of space superiority fighter, with stronger shields, better armor, and faster engines. It was armed with three laser cannons, one on each wings and one over the cockpit, with two proton torpedo launchers. The prototypes had swing wings, but Freitek went with the fixed design in the end. The fighter was slightly faster than the X-Wing and at about the same levels of maneuverable and durable.

It was a good fighter that could never outperform the X-Wing. It ended up a secondary fighter in Legends, but it was still used. After Disney purchased Lucasfilm, it was one of the designs that they kept and it has been used in several shows. However, they removed the cockpit-mounted laser, which honestly always looked pretty stupid. In both canon and Legends, the E-Wing was a versatile fighter that could take a beating, but bring its pilot and astromech back to base.

The Yuuzhan Vong War devastated the galaxy 25 years after the destruction of the Death Star in Legends. They were able to almost completely conquer the galaxy, destroying the New Republic. In its place the Galactic Alliance arose, a conglomeration of galactic powers that included the remnants of the Empire, the Bothans, the Hutts, the Hapans, and the rest. They modernized their militaries, using the lessons of the war to create new generations of old favorites, including the venerable X-Wing. Newer models like the XJ-3 and 5 made the older ones look quaint, with Incom making numerous variants, including the StealthX.

The StealthX took the XJ-3 spaceframe and smoothed out its lines. It was painted with an anti-sensor coating black paint, speckled with white to match the starfield around it. Its engines had specialized baffles so its emissions were basically non-existent. Its sensor systems were lower-powered and the comm system was basically turned off as a default. It became the fighter of choice for the Jedi, since they could use the Force as sensors and comms. They even created the shadow bomb technique (although this was first used before the StealthX was put into service in the Yuuzhan Vong War), allowing them to use the Force to push armed proton torpedoes – which had their propellant systems removed and packed with more explosives – making them even deadlier. StealthXs were optimized for Jedi, but anyone could fly them, as evidenced by legends of the cockpit Wedge Antilles and Tycho Celchu, who were able to outfly Jedi without even turning on their sensors or comms when they flew them.

The Rebel Alliance had a hard time fielding an actual fleet. While they had some capital ships – Corellian CR-series corvettes and gunships, liberated Nebulon-B frigates, jury-rigged monstrosities like the Rebel Assualt Frigate (which was what would happen if a Dreadnought -class cruiser got drunk and had a baby with a Nebulon-B ) and the Rebel Bulk Crusier, which seemed to made of scraps of every ship that could power a turbolaser battery, the Mon Calamari modified MC-series of frigates and crusiers, and various others – they didn't have them in any appreciable numbers. Remember the Rebel Fleet in Return of the Jedi ? That not one portion of the Fleet, it's the whole thing, while the Imperial Fleet there wasn't even one percent of how many capital ships the Empire could field.

The Rebels used their fighters to make up for it, launching hit and run attacks against bigger targets. Eventually, the Rebels in both canon and Legends designed the B-Wing. In Legends, it was a collab between the insectoid Verpine, some of the best shipbuilders in the galaxy, and Commander Ackbar. They designed the fighter to be slow and strong, with powerful shields and capital ship-grade weapons. Its weapons mounts were modular and it could be armed with lasers, turbolasers, autoblasters, concussion missiles, and proton torpedoes. The canon version was different; while it was built by Slayn & Korpil, the Verpine hive, it was designed by the Mon Cal Quarrie (named after Star Wars concept artist and the guy who came up with the fighter designs Ralph McQuarrie) and had what amounts to a superlaser system, with the wing cannons combining their power to fire devastating lancers of energy. Be it in canon or Legends, a B-Wing is going to survive just about anything.

What's your favorite Rebel or New Republic (or Galactic Alliance; I'm partial to Alephs and Eta Actis -5s)? Do you like canon fighters or Legends better? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.summary: As 2026 comes to an end, it is worth looking back at what this year has delivered for the anime industry, especially the masterpieces that are worth your time. Looking back, this year has been truly incredible, starting with Winter, which saw several returning anime deliver banger seasons alongside a few new additions. Spring and […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As 2026 comes to an end, it is worth looking back at what this year has delivered for the anime industry, especially the masterpieces that are worth your time. Looking back, this year has been truly incredible, starting with Winter, which saw several returning anime deliver banger seasons alongside a few new additions. Spring and Summer stood out in their own ways, and Fall continues to do the same.

Hundreds of anime have aired this year; however, not all of them have stood out. For an anime to be considered a masterpiece, it needs to do something extraordinary. That is exactly what these three anime, one from Spring and two from Summer, have achieved, earning their place as absolute masterpieces.

Smoking Behind the Supermarket With You made a special debut midway through the Spring season, with its first season consisting of just 12 episodes. With this, the series immediately ranked among the highest-rated anime on Crunchyroll , earning praise from fans. The series captivated viewers with its refreshing take on the romance genre, offering an adult perspective that most anime often lack. It achieves this through an unusual premise involving a man in his 40s who develops a companionship with a woman in her late 20s.

An even more intriguing element is how the woman portrays two different personalities: a loving supermarket clerk and a cool, hipster-dressed smoker who spends time with him behind the supermarket. Sasaki develops a different connection with each of these personalities, eventually leading to an adult friendship built on mutual understanding and advice. Honestly, the anime industry needs more series like this to broaden its horizons and attract a more mature audience.

Akane-banashi emerges as one of the most niche anime concepts ever presented, as its central premise revolves around a traditional Japanese art form called Rakugo, a method of storytelling that Western audiences may have never even heard of. However, the anime presents this concept so perfectly that it captivates viewers and is bound to spark interest in this traditional art. It achieves this by presenting Rakugo through the lens of a shonen sports anime, treating it as a competitive discipline in which multiple characters compete to earn the highest positions.

What elevates the series further is the titular protagonist , Akane, whose incredible foundation keeps the story inspiring, making her journey to earn her place in this competitive world a delight to watch. The first season offers plenty of insight into how this art form is performed and its impact on audiences. As Akane defies all odds by showcasing years of practice in pursuit of her dream, the 12 episodes of the first season never feel boring. It is the perfect time to start watching this masterpiece, especially with the new season arriving in Winter 2027.

When discussing a masterpiece, it has to be crafted in a way that captivates viewers and leaves them wanting more, and Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia does exactly that. Brought to life by Science SARU, the anime presents the story of a slave who embarks on a journey to seek revenge against the Mongol Empire after its tyranny takes the lives of everyone she loves. However, as Sitara becomes more deeply involved in the Mongol Empire, several layers of nuance are unveiled, making it much more than a simple revenge story.

It eventually evolves into a political game within the vast empire, with royals turning against each other to secure higher positions, while Sitara finds herself caught in the middle. The revenge narrative also gradually transforms into a story about saving someone new she has grown to care for, while characters positioned as villains reveal their better sides, leaving viewers to decide whom to support. It reaches the level of masterpiece TV shows like Game of Thrones , and for anyone who enjoys that kind of storytelling, Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia is one of the first anime masterpieces of 2026 to deliver a similar experience, with elements that make it even better.

What anime of 2026 has made you feel immersed in its story and earned a place among the masterpieces everyone should watch? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.title: Jesse Plemons on the ‘Honor’ of Playing Plutarch in 'The Hunger Games' After Philip Seymour Hoffman and Debating Director Francis Lawrence Over the Character's Motivations
articles.summary: “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” might be Haymitch Abernathy’s prequel movie, but Oscar nominee Jesse Plemons was the first person cast in the film. Plemons plays Plutarch Heavensbee, a Capitol insider, who becomes a key figure in the rebellion that sparks in the latter half of Suzanne Collins’ original trilogy of dystopian novels. […]
articles.content:
“ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ” might be Haymitch Abernathy’s prequel movie, but Oscar nominee Jesse Plemons was the first person cast in the film.

Plemons plays Plutarch Heavensbee, a Capitol insider, who becomes a key figure in the rebellion that sparks in the latter half of Suzanne Collins’ original trilogy of dystopian novels. In the second book, “Catching Fire,” and its 2013 film adaptation, Plutarch is introduced as the Head Gamemaker, tasked with creating the brutal trials in the Hunger Games. (The late Philip Seymour Hoffman originated the role.) At the end of that story, Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) learns that Plutarch was really scheming from inside the establishment to help support the rebels. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories James Talarico Crashes ‘SNL’ Cold Open: ‘I’m the Guy Who’s Been Texting You Every Day Asking for $5’ ‘SNL’ Sets Timothée Chalamet and Robert De Niro as Final Hosts of 2026

But “Sunrise on the Reaping” takes place 25 years before those events, so casting the younger Plutarch was key.

“I’m a huge fan of Jesse’s,” franchise director Francis Lawrence tells Variety . “Had never worked with him before, and had always wanted to, and thought he would be perfect.”

Plemons, of course, is one of the blockbuster movie’s most accomplished stars — one of the star-studded ensemble’s seven Oscar nominees: Jennifer Lawrence and Kieran Culkin are winners, with Glenn Close receiving an honorary Oscar earlier this month.

“We had a lot of fun casting all these people fans are familiar with for this movie. But with [Plutarch] specifically, there was a lot more development,” Lawrence adds, sharing that he and "Hunger Games" producer Nina Jacobson spent considerable time working with Collins on Plutarch’s arc. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“He’s an infiltrator,” Lawrence explains. “He’s the guy at the beginning of the formation of the resistance, and at the same time, has to get to the place where by ‘Catching Fire’ he’s at Snow’s side and so trusted. So, it was on us to figure out how to portray Plutarch in a way that is believable. And that was fun because we were adding scenes that weren’t in the book.”

Book readers might’ve noticed a new Plutarch scene in the “Sunrise on the Reaping” movie — where Plemons appears bruised and bloodied after being brutally interrogated by President Snow (Ralph Fiennes), who’s learned of a secret plot to sabotage the 50th Hunger Games.

“That was a keystone scene for us, and we went over and over and over different approaches of it,” Lawrence says. “How can we have him be active on these two distinct paths: one is, ‘How can I keep this resistance alive, but a secret?’ And ‘How can I seem utterly loyal and faithful to Snow, who is very, very smart?’ It’s become one of my favorite scenes in the movie.”

Lawrence kicked off conversations with Plemons by sending Collins’ unpublished manuscript. The actor cracked open the book, but because he was also working on “Digger,” he hadn’t made it to the final pages before the finished script came in.

“I read the script, and then finished the book, and was surprised by how engaging it was and how complex the character was,” Plemons tells Variety over the phone from his home in Texas. “And I was really blown away by the script and the book.”

Indeed, Plutarch is a meaty character. But he also had to consider that the role was originated by Hoffman, one of his favorite actors of all time, who'd also played his father in 2012’s “The Master.” As such, Plemons knew saying yes would come with plenty of questions from reporters about how it felt to continue the late Hoffman’s “legacy” after the actor’s unexpected death in 2014. Even after filming the part, Plemons hasn’t quite ironed out how to articulate his feelings on such a lofty question.

“That's a tough one to answer,” Plemons replies, thoughtfully, when I ask how he feels about all of that. “I’m definitely honored to have the opportunity to play this character. I wish I had a better answer for you, but it’s complicated.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Less complicated are his feelings about the “Hunger Games” franchise’s larger message, which was a key factor in his decision to take the part.

“I find it a big accomplishment when a film or a book that has such a wide appeal is able to tackle real-world themes and issues everyone feels and relates to, that connect to all of our lives,” Plemons says.

Read on as Plemons explains how he approached Plutarch’s prequel arc, including what he garnered from Hoffman’s performance, and why he and Lawrence debated over the complex character’s true motivations.

Many things. One, just the nature of doing a prequel like this. It was interesting knowing where the character ends up and how all these relationships progress, and then realizing there was actually more space to play and create ourselves. To fill in this very large blank over the course of 25 years. And there was something, just in the scope of the amount of time that he has been fighting and infiltrating the capital, there's a sort of double agent aspect.

There's a sort of philosopher side to him. There's most definitely an importance on knowledge that he's trying to instill in Haymitch. And at the same time, what I was most interested in was his very pragmatic sense of hope, which is not at all shrouded in any sort of rose-colored idealism. It's very rooted in the reality of how difficult and almost impossible it's going to be, and I was just really intrigued by that on a personal level.

The other interesting aspect is that he winds up being with the good guys, the resistance. But even still, in his relationship with Haymitch, I feel like I was constantly questioning — and I feel like the audience probably will too — just how expendable he feels Haymitch is for the greater good. All the while, he's at least, to me, growing pretty fond of him as the story goes on. So there were just a lot of complexities that I really enjoyed.

That was the first sequence I shot, which was great. It's obvious he's incredibly intelligent. He's able to sort of play this role. And I really loved that sequence with Glenn [Close]. I'm assuming they've known each other practically all of Plutarch’s life; she’s probably like a crazy aunt in some way. And it was really fun to play with maniuplating Drusilla without her knowing it.

It's interesting. Obviously, his agenda is to prove himself to Snow and everyone in the Capitol. And at the same time, there must be something kind of alluring about pulling this [rebellion] off. It was really interesting, and Francis definitely allowed for some space, especially in the sequence where we're filming Haymitch saying goodbye. We brought in a little more of the book there and a little more of Plutarch handling the camera operator, being a little more hands-on than was in the scene.

That scene, because it was a new addition that wasn't in the book, was something that I could definitely see the need for — to see where Plutarch was in all of this. Aside from seeing in the library earlier on, it’s the only time you get to see Plutarch with Snow, and it was just an absolute thrill getting to work with Ralph.

It's such a game of intellect between the two. Plutarch is trying to gauge how much Snow knows, whether he knows that he's involved and who he knows is involved. At the same time, he’s trying to double down and act as if he's truly working in the interest of the Capitol. We played around a lot with that scene.

I don't think there's like a black-or-white, or cut-and-dry, easy way of categorizing Plutarch or his motivations. The main debate Francis and I were in was whether or not his motivations were rooted in some sort of self-centeredness. A kind of wanting to be the hero, or just wanting to stick it to the Capitol and his family, that I'm sure, as a child, he had very conflicted feelings about.

I felt his intentions were pure. The fact that he would like to stick it to the Capitol, that's most definitely part of it. He's most definitely entitled and privileged. But I think everyone's given a choice, and at some point, Plutarch decided that knowledge is of the utmost importance, and I think, morally, he is very much on the side of what is right and he sees the injustice. I believe his intentions are pure. I just don't know why you would make it all that time if your motivations were about your own self-interest.

I had a lot of conversations with some of the other actors that were playing characters that were established in the other films, and we all had our own unique challenges and thoughts about how best to capture that essence, while at the same time taking some freedom in the fact that 24-25 years is a long time. The thing that jumped out at me in the film that he was in [Hoffman first appeared in 2013's "Catching Fire"] was that they were still most definitely fully committed to the cause, but you could see the time. You could see the weariness of all those characters.

There were little things that I was conscious of and tried to connect to his performance, but for the most part, I felt like this is a very different Plutarch. He’s beginning his journey and is incredibly ambitious, and the whole energy of his pursuit just felt very different, and all the relationships, like his relationship with Snow, are just beginning. So, it wound up feeling like there was quite a bit of room.

Most definitely. I can't imagine where her mind will go next — no one can. But, personally, selfishly, what I would love to see is Plutarch's teenage years. I thought a lot about that while we were shooting, but I don't think I could play that part.

[Laughs.] Like “The Irishman.”

This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity.

articles.title: Doomsday’s New Avengers Star Isn’t Sure How She Fits Into The Story Either: “No Clue Where I Will Be”

There are a lot of heroes in the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe movie, including Sam Wilson's Avengers, the New Avengers who were once called the Thunderbolts, the Fantastic Four, the X-Men, and the Wakandans. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Florence Pugh has responded to Kevin Feige's comments that Yelena Belova will be an "anchor" in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday movie. There are a lot of heroes in the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe movie, including Sam Wilson's Avengers, the New Avengers who were once called the Thunderbolts, the Fantastic Four, the X-Men, and the Wakandans. That is a lot of characters to balance in the movie, and Feige has said that the entire Avengers: Doomsday movie will be anchored by Yelena Belova .

When hearing what Feige said about her role in the movie, Pugh was surprised. “Like a literal anchor? She’s chained to all these characters, and they can’t go anywhere? It’s honestly such a massive operation that I have no clue where I will be in this storyline," Pugh said in a new Empire magazine interview. "You can’t even fathom that what you’re gonna do is gonna anchor anything, so it’s wonderful to hear that he thinks that.”

Florence Pugh on Kevin Feige saying that Yelena Belova will serve as an “anchor” in ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’: “Like a literal anchor? She’s chained to all these characters and they can’t go anywhere? It’s honestly such a massive operation that I have no clue where I will be in this… pic.twitter.com/BzKthdzA9G

While it might seem like a surprise that Yelena Belova is the anchor of the new Avengers movie, it does make sense. Yelena is the sister of Black Widow, who was one of the original members of the Avengers. Natasha had a strong connection to heroes like Thor and Steve Rogers, and Black Widow fought alongside others such as Sam Wilson's Captain America and Bucky Barnes' Winter Soldier. Yelena is also someone who has suffered great loss, and her character arc in Thunderbolts* was all about her coming to terms with the fact that she lives with so much grief.

She was last seen in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , where she helped Peter Parker get what he needed for his battle to stop Jean Grey. She even saw the sadness that Peter Parker had, and she showed more empathy than almost anyone in the MCU to this point. As a member of the New Avengers and as someone who has at least a loose connection with Steve Rogers and Thor, Yelena has something in common with two of the biggest factions in this upcoming war. Add in the fact that she knows Kate Bishop thanks to their relationship in the Hawkeye series, and this could add another connection in the movie.

Someone has to bring all these heroes together, and while it seems that will come down to Thor and Steve Rogers, Yelena Belova is the one person who has learned what it means to be a teammate and help others. She had to learn this the hard way, from her trauma in the Black Widow movie to coming to terms with Natasha's death in Hawkeye and then learning to work as a team in the Thunderbolts. Yelena Belova is one of the best characters introduced in the MCU after Avengers: Infinity War , and if she is getting pushed to the forefront of the new story, no one deserves it more.

articles.content:
With the release of the prequel The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping , franchise producer Nina Jacobson regrets splitting the Mockingjay films into two parts.

At the time,  The Twilight Saga  and Harry Potter split their grand finale into two films, and Lionsgate followed suit, breaking up the last Suzanne Collins book of the OG Hunger Games trilogy into two films as well.

"Even though I love the Mockingjay films, if I had it to do over again, I think both Francis [Lawrence, director] and I might try to do it all in one," she said in an interview with Empire .

She continued, " Mockingjay was such a big book, and it takes you to so many different places. But in the end, I think that Francis and I both felt that splitting them up… even if it did come from an inside-out place of really feeling like we needed two films to tell the story, I think audiences find it cynical. Even if its intentions are earnest, which they were. articles.title: Patrick Stewart's Legacy Is Finding an Unexpected Home in Magic: The Gathering, With Signed Cards Fetching Huge Prices
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s relatively recent foray into the canon of other franchises— such as Marvel Comics, Final Fantasy, or Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles—has been controversial since its inception. The first legal black-bordered set of “Universes Beyond” cards came with the release of the Walking Dead from Secret Lair in October of 2020, and the reaction […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Magic: The Gathering’ s relatively recent foray into the canon of other franchises— such as Marvel Comics , Final Fantasy, or Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles—has been controversial since its inception. The first legal black-bordered set of “Universes Beyond” cards came with the release of the Walking Dead from Secret Lair in October of 2020, and the reaction online was dramatic. In an official statement from the Commander Rules Committee, level five judge Sheldon Menery said that the response was “at times, quite overwhelming.”

Thousands sought to make their voice heard, raising every issue from the difficulty of acquiring these unique cards, to protecting the sanctity of Magic: The Gathering ’s story IP. Many of these issues were solved, others dissolved—the IP problem for example can be compellingly reframed as a way to bring new players into the community. However, with the release of collaboration between Magic: The Gathering and iconic nerd property Star Trek , a brave new problem has reared its ugly head.

Sir Patrick Stewart was one of the most well-respected and well-liked actors of our era. His incredible acting range allowed him to feel at home playing parts in both critically acclaimed productions of Shakespeare, and in Elder Scrolls: Oblivion. His recent death sent shockwaves through a number of communities, and the thoughts of fans are still with the friends and family he left behind . 

The design team at Wizard of the Coast could not have predicted this eventuality, and given his widespread fame it was only natural that his Star Trek character, Jean-Luc Picard, would appear on a number of cards, with 23 different cards representing Stewart’s likeness in their art. The cards include alternative art reprints of staples like Kenrith, the Returned King , the star of the “Federation Fleet" preconstructed deck , and one of the much sought after headliners—a copy of Captain Jean-Luc Picard personally signed by the actor himself.

The question raised is morbid but obvious; has Stewart’s tragic death unfairly and unnaturally buoyed the price of these already valuable cards? Online prices records seem to indicate the answer is yes. On October 28th, immediately following the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart, cards like Captain Jean-Luc Picard shot up from around 17 dollars to nearly 60 before dipping back down into the realm of reason. 

The issue of signed cards is particularly thorny, as only 250 will ever be produced, and this will be one of the last items ever signed by the actor. As of time of writing, listings for the card have risen as high as $30,000. Any player of any trading card game can tell you that scalpers are a problem endemic to the genre—for them, this could be a goldmine, the perfect excuse to hike up the resale value. Scalpers must bulk buy their products from Wizards of Coast, meaning that both groups may in effect be profiting off of the death of Sir Patrick Stewart.

This highlights some of the biggest problems identified with Universes Beyond—When you use materials from franchises from a completely different medium, utilizing real world actors, you have much less control over your own press. As of yet, the actual effects of these unforeseen circumstances are completely unknown. If Wizards of the Coast takes extra measures in future to prevent this kind of disrespectful profiteering, the issue may be avoided entirely. It is certainly not the fault of any member of the team, and harassment of those involved would be an even bigger insult to the memory of a hero; as Picard said himself, “It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness; that is life.”

What's your reaction to this jump in price? What does it say about Sir Patrick Stewart's legacy? Share your thoughts in the comments!

articles.title: David Fincher Teases Fifth Brad Pitt Collaboration, And It Would Be a New Genre for Him
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Sony After four movies together, Brad Pitt and David Fincher are looking to take their partnership into a new dimension: animation. The two recently reunited for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, their first movie together in 18 years. While both men have worked in animation, the project they're discussing would mark Fincher's debut as the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After four movies together, Brad Pitt and David Fincher are looking to take their partnership into a new dimension: animation. The two recently reunited for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , their first movie together in 18 years. While both men have worked in animation, the project they're discussing would mark Fincher's debut as the director of an animated feature.

During an appearance on The Big Picture podcast (via The Playlist ), Fincher revealed that he and Pitt had discussed several projects in the years between movies. Among them was what Fincher believes could be the scariest movie ever made. Even the star of Seven had reservations about making that movie. For their animated movie, the technically ambitious filmmaker wants to experiment with a hybrid approach to animation, using Pitt's physical performance as a reference for the animators without resorting to rotoscoping. Fincher has yet to reveal anything about the plot of the movie.

Fincher and Deadpool director Tim Miller are executive producers of Netflix's animated anthology series Love, Death & Robots . Fincher made his animated directorial debut with the third season episode "Bad Travelling." Based on a short story by Neal Asher, the episode follows the crew of a ship that finds itself at the mercy of a giant, man-eating crustacean. Fincher returned to direct the fourth season's "Can't Stop," which recreates a Red Hot Chili Peppers concert with the members of the band depicted as marionettes.

Before making his feature directorial debut with Alien 3 , Fincher worked at Industrial Light & Magic on movies including Return of the Jedi and Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom . His background in visual effects came in particularly handy when he reunited with Pitt for 2008's The Curious Case of Benjamin Button . The technology developed to digitally age Pitt earned the movie an Academy Award for Best Visual Effects. Pitt's two biggest roles in animated movies were both for DreamWorks Animation. The actor voiced the title character in 2003's Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas and played Metro Man, the superhero whose apparent death leaves the title character of Megamind without a purpose.

As much as fans of Seven and Fight Club might like to see the two make another thriller together, animation could give Fincher the opportunity to work in genres he hasn't explored in decades. The filmmaker spent years developing an adaptation of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas for Disney that never made it into production.

It'll be interesting to see how receptive audiences are to Fincher experimenting with animation given the controversy surrounding his use of AI in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . In the same interview, Fincher discussed using AI in post-production to clean up dialogue and potentially alter the movements of actors' mouths, allowing him to combine dialogue from one take with footage from another. The director has yet to address some of the other allegations regarding the use of generative AI in the movie.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is currently playing in IMAX theaters and will debut on Netflix on December 23rd.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Vampires have been making a major comeback in popular media in recent years, with films, games, and anime reinventing the nocturnal blood-suckers to bring them back into the limelight. 2027 is ramping up to be a big year for the gothic creatures, with vampire-themed anime like Otaku Vampire's Love Bite and The Record of a Fallen Vampire set to release throughout the year. Joining them is a brand-new series from Studio Teddy, the anime adaptation of Mercedes and the Waning Moon , an original series by Firehead that marries the concepts of isekai adventure with the romantic appeal of vampirism.

Mercedes and the Waning Moon is a unique spin on the isekai genre, taking a disgruntled, unnamed reincarnated individual and giving them a second chance at life as a vampire named Mercedes Grunewald, a descendant of vampire nobility forced to live in the countryside with her mother due to bad blood between her father. Unsure of her future or position in their house's line of succession, Mercedes instead becomes a professional dungeon crawler. In anticipation for the anime's January release and kicking off the new year, the anime adaptation revealed a stunning new trailer and promotional art you can find below.

The newly revealed trailer and key visual for Mercedes and the Waning Room depicts the titular Mercedes wielding her signature battle axe while surrounded by shattered glass teasing other characters that appear throughout the series. The main voice cast for the anime was also shared, which includes a star-studded cast consisting of Anna Nagase (Akane in Akane-banashi ) as Mercedes, Kenta Miyake (All Might in My Hero Academia ) as Benkei, Ryunosuke Watanuki (Okuhito in Blue Lock ) as Kuro, Junichi Suwabe (Eraser Head in My Hero Academia ) as Florian, Ai Kayano (Mikan in Danganronpa 2 ) as Ludia, Hina Omori as Margit, Miyu Tomita (Riko in Made in Abyss ) as Monica, and Sho Hayami (Sosuke in Bleach ) as Bernhard.

The anime adaptation of Firehead's original series will be produced by Studio Teddy, an independent anime studio founded in 2014. A relatively newer studio, Teddy previously produced the main animation for I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level Season 2, with Mercedes and the Waning Moon being their first original animation project, but the studio has worked on a number of heavy-hitting anime series in a smaller capacity.

These other projects include key animation on Jujutsu Kaisen Season 2, key animation across multiple entries in the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure franchise, and animation assistance on Sailor Moon Crystal . If that weren't promising enough that Mercedes and the Waning Moon is going to be a hit, the director for the series is none other than Kunihisa Sugishima, best known for his work on Yu Gi Oh! Duel Monsters , as well as storyboarding credits on Code Geass and Higurashi .

Mercedes and the Waning Moon will officially release as part of the Winter 2027 Anime season on Sundays beginning on January 10, 2027. As of writing, there is currently no official announcement when a global streaming service like Crunchyroll or HIDIVE will be picking up the anime to stream for global audiences. However, the original light novel series has been picked up and localized for English-speaking audiences by J-Novel Club. Available digitally under the title Mercedes and the Waning Moon: The Dungeoneering Feats of a Discarded Vampire Aristocrat , the first four volumes of the series are currently available directly through the publishers site for purchase as an e-book.

Originally a web novel written by Firehead that was uploaded to Shosetsuka ni Naro between 2018 to 2022, the Mercedes and the Waning Moon was eventually picked up for a print release by TO Books who collected the series into light novels and began publishing the books in 2021. The series is still ongoing, and has a manga adaptation that condenses the story into a graphic novel format. The manga is also available in English through J-Novel Club.

As of writing, even before the anime adaptaiton makes its official debut, Mercedes and the Waning Moon has an extremely impressive 200,000 copies in circulation. But how do you like the look of the new anime so far? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments!

articles.title: I Am Legend Director Blasts Ending of Will Smith's 2007 Blockbuster, "It's a Bit of a Failure"
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. I Am Legend director Francis Lawrence has finally admitted that the ending of the Will Smith movie I Am Legend was a "bit of a failure." I Am Legend was controversial when it was released because fans of the source novel objected to how the movie changed the story's ending, which changed its overall meaning. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google I Am Legend director Francis Lawrence has finally admitted that the ending of the Will Smith movie I Am Legend was a "bit of a failure." I Am Legend was controversial when it was released because fans of the source novel objected to how the movie changed the story's ending, which changed its overall meaning. The movie was based on the novel of the same name by Richard Matheson , and it had been made as a movie twice before with the titles The Last Man on Earth and The Omega Man . It is a post-apocalyptic thriller with a man trying to survive an outbreak that turned most survivors into vampires. The novel was about how the man realized he was now the monster by the end.

In a new interview on the Team Deakins podcast, director Francis Lawrence said, "I’m really proud of the first hour of that movie. But the last 40 minutes, where the creatures end up becoming a big part of it, I think it’s a bit of a failure, honestly, and we just didn’t approach it the way that we should have and could have."

The End of I Am Legend Betrays Its Core Themes Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. The name of the novel, I Am Legend , signifies that the hero of the story, Neville, realized that he was actually the monster in this world. He was hunting down the vampires and killing them during the day. However, readers were led to believe all the infected were like the undead vampires attacking his house, when there were also infected who were not undead. Neville believed he was the hero in his story, but he was only a murderer killing the new dominant species on the planet, a species that just wanted to survive in peace. However, the readers were led to believe they were evil because they kept tormenting Neville at his house. When he realized at the end that he was the monster and they were only fighting back. He said, "I am legend," before he died, meaning he is now the urban myth that the new species would be taught to fear.

Lawrence's movie was all about Neville and other survivors finding a cure and fixing the vampire-zombie hybrids in the movie. By "fixing" something that wasn't a problem but was just the evolution of the species, it went completely against what this story was really about. Lawrence also talked about the comparison to the novel, and he said that an alternate ending played into it better. He also touched on how he had to change the ending, which originally had Neville leaving the infected woman to the monsters, while leaving with Anna and Ethan. He said test audiences hated that ending, and they had to change it one month before the film's release, with only three days of reshoots.

In the theatrical ending, Neville gives Anna and Ethan the cure, which works, and then he sacrifices himself with a grenade to kill the vampire-zombie hybrids who were attacking them. However, there was an alternate ending on the DVD that got it right, where Neville realizes that the infected are only trying to protect their own, and he returns the female companion he had captured for his experiments, and they allow him to live as a result. It still lost the idea that he was the monster, but it was at least closer.

What are your thoughts on I Am Legend and its two endings? Let us know which one you think works better in the comments below.

articles.title: Forget Inception, This is Christopher Nolan's Best Sci-Fi Movie & I Can Explain Why
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. Christopher Nolan has thrived in the sci-fi genre, both with his Dark Knight trilogy and his later films, including the Oscar-nominated Inception. With titles like Interstellar and Tenet to his name, it is clear that sci-fi remains one of Nolan's favored genres, and he has helped bring mainstream audiences to see stories they normally wouldn't […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Christopher Nolan has thrived in the sci-fi genre, both with his Dark Knight trilogy and his later films, including the Oscar-nominated Inception . With titles like Interstellar and Tenet to his name, it is clear that sci-fi remains one of Nolan's favored genres, and he has helped bring mainstream audiences to see stories they normally wouldn't pay to see. He is the third-highest-grossing filmmaker of all time, and he remains one of the few directors today who can sell a movie just based on his name alone. However, his best sci-fi movie is one that not enough people talk about.

In 2006, Nolan released the sci-fi thriller The Prestige , and it remains one of his best films and the highest-quality sci-fi movie of his career. While the story seems like a historical thriller about rival magicians, it features twists and turns that place it solidly in the sci-fi genre, and it hits on every single level.

The Prestige Is Christopher Nolan's Best Sci-Fi Movie Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. On the surface, The Prestige looks like a historical thriller based in the real world. The movie stars Hugh Jackman and Christian Bale as Robert Angier and Alfred Borden, rival magicians who become hated enemies after Angier's wife, Julia (Piper Perabo), dies during a trick gone wrong. The two men then set out on a mission to one-up each other, while Angier has more ominous plans in store for Borden, with help from real-life inventor Nikola Tesla (David Bowie), and a strong mix of sci-fi storytelling.

As with all Nolan's movies, this one plays with time. It is similar to his debut movie, Following, in that the film plays out of order, with the scenes bouncing around the timeline between the present day and the past, and it isn't until the end that the movie shows how Angier was able to pull off his seemingly impossible tricks that brought down Borden. However, what really made this movie great was that both magicians revealed their impressive tricks, Borden using a practical real-world trick called "The Transported Man," and Angier using sci-fi methods, with each trick having the same ultimate result.

Sadly, the movie wasn't a huge success, although it did make $109 million on a $40 million budget. This was before Nolan was a monster success at the box office, and if the movie had come out just four years later, it could have been a massive hit. Instead, four years later, Nolan released Inception , and that was the sci-fi movie that earned him high praise and Oscar recognition. If the release dates for Inception and The Prestige had been reversed, both would still be recognized today as masterpieces, but more people would recognize the brilliance of The Prestige . It never needs the visual tricks of Inception and tells a brilliant story on a smaller scale, and it deserves much more credit than it gets.

One very notable thing about The Prestige and Inception is that both share one common trait. Christopher Nolan made both movies while taking a break from his Dark Knight trilogy. He released The Prestige in 2006, one year after Batman Begins but two years before The Dark Knight . He then released Inception in 2010 , two years after The Dark Knight and two years before The Dark Knight Rises . They gave Nolan a chance to make something very different and original in between his superhero epics. While Inception was an original idea, The Prestige was based on the novel by Christopher Priest, but as something that most fans don't know about, Nolan was still able to make it his own.

Nolan was also able to use both familiar actors from his movies and some faces that comic book fans would recognize down the line. As mentioned, The Prestige starred Hugh Jackman, who previously played Wolverine in the X-Men movies, and Christian Bale, who played Batman in the Dark Knight trilogy. On top of Bale, Nolan also brought over Michael Caine, who played Alfred in the Dark Knight films and the stage engineer for Angier and Borden in The Prestige . Scarlett Johansson played Angier and Borden's assistant years before she joined the MCU as Black Widow. Finally, Andy Serkis starred as Nikola Tesla's assistant nearly a decade before he played Ulysses Klaue in the MCU.

It seemed this was not only a break for Nolan from superhero fare but also a break for Bale and Caine, who had a chance to do something completely different in this period piece. While I won't mention how the movie went into the realm of sci-fi to avoid spoilers, it was a nice twist at the end that really showed how masterful Nolan was at crafting his stories, allowing them to build to the big reveals, and never leaving the audience feeling cheated. The Prestige is Nolan's best sci-fi movie, which says a lot in a career that has seen more than one masterpiece.

What are your thoughts on Christopher Nolan's The Prestige ? Let us know your favorite Nolan sci-fi movie in the comments below.

Jesse Eisenberg is reflecting on his work in Hollywood and why he has a very different experience with fans in public than some other actors.

In a new interview with The New Yorker , the actor, director, writer, and producer of The Debut said fans of his work are "mostly fine" when they see him in public, as his roles are not sexualized.

Luca Guadagnino wants to return to romance.

Speaking to Variety at the Marrakech Film Festival where he's presenting "Artificial," the Italian filmmaker behind “Call Me by Your Name,” “Bones and All” and “Queer” revealed that he hopes his next directorial endeavor will be another love story.

“I think a lot of inspiration could come from facts of history,” Guadagnino said when asked what he would like to explore in his next film. “I want to make another love story, so I have to think about it, but I want to make a kind movie, another love story.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Sweden’s Oscar Entry 'Adult Supervision' Closes Further Deals (EXCLUSIVE) Marvel’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Won’t Screen for BAFTA, Golden Globes and Other Early Awards Groups to Guard Its Spoilers (EXCLUSIVE)

He also confirmed that two of his previously announced projects — a new adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’ “American Psycho” and the gay romance “Separate Rooms” — are no longer moving forward with him.

“Separate Rooms" was set to be an adaptation of Italian writer Pier Vittorio Tondelli’s 1989 novel about a writer grappling with the death of his lover. Josh O’Connor, who previously worked with Guadagnino on “Challengers,” and Léa Seydoux had been linked to the project since 2024.

“I don’t think I’m doing a movie with Léa Seydoux, unfortunately. That’s not happening,” Guadagnino said. “But I would love to work with Léa, of course.”

The director also addressed the demise of his “American Psycho” adaptation, which was first announced by Lionsgate in October 2024. The film, penned by Scott Z. Burns, was intended to be a fresh interpretation of Ellis’ 1991 novel rather than a remake of Mary Harron’s 2000 cult classic starring Christian Bale. “That’s the job of a director," he said of its dissolution. The filmmaker also dispelled speculation that Robert Pattinson had been in contention to play Patrick Bateman, though he said "he’s a perfect choice for James Bond," adding: "He's an incredible star, he's done so many great roles and I wish someday to work with him, of course."

Would Guadagnino direct a Bond film? “I would say yes, yes, of course,” he said of the prospect. “I would like to play with icons.”

The director's upcoming film, “Artificial,” marks another departure from the sweeping romances that have come to define much of his oeuvre.
