SNL surprised fans earlier this season with a David S Pumpkins sketch to celebrate the off-beat spooky character’s tenth anniversary. Current cast member Mikey Day was joined by his OG co-stars Tom Hanks and Bobby Moynihan for what hilariously turned out to be several minutes of freezing in place while James Austin Johnson paused the sketch for his President Trump impression. The bit went over very well with fans at home, but it turns out the broadcast version contained a key change suggested by Tom Hanks who was looking out for everyone’s bodies.

Here’s how Moynihan described the conversation he had with Hanks after dress rehearsal to Mashable …

Moynihan said they probably would have figured all of this out before dress rehearsal, but they actually weren't paying much attention to the larger sketch. Instead, they spent like an hour talking about how absolutely absurd they felt being back in the costumes David S Pumpkins and the Skeletons, who have their own wild names . None of them ever thought the original sketch was going to hit, let alone lead to a TV special and an anniversary sketch a decade later.

That’s the power of SNL though. Some of the sketches that go viral and live on in people’s memories involve sharp political commentary or really thoughtful parodies of society. Others just involve a goofy character or characters that connect with people for whatever reason . David S Pumpkins and the Skeletons are definitely examples of those characters. They’re just so over the top and ridiculous that you can’t look away, even if they’re frozen in the background of a President Trump sketch and trying to stay as still as possible.

articles.title: X-Men Favorite Confirms MCU Crossover Was Something He Believed Would Never Happen

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the best moments in the Avengers: Doomsday final trailer was when James Marsden's Cyclops said the iconic line, "To me, my X-Men." It was something that most fans never believed they would see, especially with the original trilogy's cast returning for the big Marvel Cinematic Universe reunion. You can add Marsden to the list of people who never thought this could ever happen, for several reasons. In the trailer, there was a huge moment where all the heroes gathered together with the Avengers, Fantastic Four, and X-Men preparing to battle, and it was Cyclops who got the big crowd-friendly line.

In an interview with Entertainment Weekly , Marsden said he didn’t know whether or not to believe it at first, because "there was so much chatter over however many years about doing another film and bringing them into this universe, and it never really came to fruition… But then, ‘Hey, Kevin wants to chat with you.’ You’re thinking this has gotta be real. It’s not just ‘shoot the s—.’"

X-Men Actor Said Avengers: Doomsday Is for the Fans Image Courtesy of Marvel This is a huge moment for James Marsden because of how he went out in the original X-Men trilogy. After Bryan Singer left the franchise to make Superman Returns , and Marsden signed on for a small role in that film, the X-Men movies moved on from him in the worst way possible. In X-Men: The Last Stand, Jean Grey killed him off-screen early in the movie, taking out one of the most important X-Men leaders in the least satisfying way possible. That ended Marsden's run as Cyclops, and the hero was gone until the later prequels, when Tye Sheridan took over the role as a young Scott Summers.

It seemed that Marsden was finished with the franchise, and it came as a surprise when Kevin Feige called him and offered him the chance to return. When talking about the return, he said that it was bigger than just returning to the role. Marsden talked about getting to wear the classic blue-and-yellow Cyclops uniform instead of the all-black costumes that the team wore in the 2000s movies. He said it was "one of those pinch-me moments" and it gave fans "everything that they want to see." However, the one thing that bothered him about the new costume was the visor, which he said wasn't practical since it severely limited his vision.

The new Avengers: Doomsday movie looks like it will be the beginning of the end for this lineup of the X-Men . Since the comic book stories showed every Earth in the multiverse destroyed before Doctor Doom rebuilt a new world in his image, the X-Men's world is going to die. While it was thought that the X-Men would die in this movie, there are rumors that some of them will be back in Avengers: Secret Wars, and for many fans, this could give them a chance to see Cyclops finally treated with the respect he deserves.

articles.summary: HBO's Harry Potter is trying to be a Christmas gift to the world, but the series does have a fair amount of skepticism to overcome first. No matter how you feel about the TV series reboot, however, you can't deny that HBO is investing heavily in Harry Potter, trying to give viewers the full experience […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google HBO's Harry Potter is trying to be a Christmas gift to the world, but the series does have a fair amount of skepticism to overcome first. No matter how you feel about the TV series reboot, however, you can't deny that HBO is investing heavily in Harry Potter , trying to give viewers the full experience of the books via a long-form television format. That means more characters, story arcs, and lore than the Harry Potter films could hold, but also a lot more fine detail required to realize the show.

As the promotional campaign for Harry Potter kicks into high gear, HBO is rolling out an entire (almost re-educational) informational campaign, which highlights all the many details and Easter eggs the creative team put into the project.

Comedic actor Nick Frost ( Shaun of the Dead, Hot Fuzz ) is stepping into Harry Potter to play Hagrid, the lovable half-giant who is the groundskeeper at Hogwarts, and becomes like a surrogate uncle to Harry, being the first one to introduce the boy to the Wizarding World. While being interviewed about the show, Frost shared his experience of walking onto one of the most amazing sets he's ever seen.

If you know the story of the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (which has inspired the first season of the show), then you know that one of the most pivotal developments in the book is when Harry and his friends discover Voldemort in the Forbidden Forest outside of Hogwarts. The evil wizard is trying to preserve his fading life by hunting down, killing, and drinking a unicorn's blood – only to have Harry and Co. catch him in the act and nearly discover the identity of Voldemort's secret disciple/mole inside Hogwarts.

As Nick Frost revealed, HBO has built an actual forest as part of the Hogwarts set. It's not just an impressive recreation of the Forbidden Forest: it's a living set that will grow over the presumably 7 seasons of the Harry Potter series!

"Hunting down the unicorn blood in the Forbidden Forest was great. They’ve built a massive forest in the set that’s going to be there for 10 years," Frost explained to the Harry Potter official site. "They’re calling it a living set because it grows as we shoot… there’s a stream in there, and there’s hills. It’s absolutely nuts. Once I got in there and knew I was going to spend two weeks hunting down a unicorn or we might come across Voldemort, that was fantastic. That whole portion of the shoot was great."

As stated: HBO is making a high-dollar, long-term investment in Harry Potter , and the Forbidden Forest is just one part of it. Give Nick Frost's interview a read in its entirety to learn even more.

Harry Potter will premiere on HBO on Christmas Day.

articles.title: 5 Times Superheroes Had to Save Thanksgiving, Because Even Villains Don't Take Holidays Off
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Thanksgiving is often a time for family gatherings and relaxation, but supervillains don't take holidays off, so there have always been comic book stories where the heroes had to save the day over the holidays. This was true with everyone from Batman to Daredevil, and in every case, the stories found a way to tie […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Thanksgiving is often a time for family gatherings and relaxation, but supervillains don't take holidays off, so there have always been comic book stories where the heroes had to save the day over the holidays. This was true with everyone from Batman to Daredevil, and in every case, the stories found a way to tie the themes of family and fellowship into the story of a superhero trying to bring down a supervillain to save the holidays. Of course, Thanksgiving is an American holiday in November, and the stories that come out concerning that special day are almost always lined up to coincide with the celebration.

What makes many of the Thanksgiving superhero stories so great is that the heroes are either trying to celebrate with their families or helping make sure that others can celebrate in peace. The bad thing is, villains don't care, and if they disrupt family dinners, all the better.

The team of child heroes Power Pack had a pretty emotional Thanksgiving storyline that played out in Power Pack #18-19 (1985) by Louise Simonson, Brent Anderson, and Scott Williams. The two stories were titled "Kurse" and "Guess Who's Coming to Dinner," and while the first issue was about the superhero battles on Thanksgiving, the second was about the fallout for the Power family. This was a tough time because their mother was in the hospital, and most of the Powers kids didn't want to celebrate Thanksgiving at all.

Issue #18 was a "Secret Wars II" crossover where the Beyonder-powered Dark Elf Kurse injured their mom, and the kids were unable to beat him until Thor and Beta Ray Bill showed up to help. Young Katie invited several of their superhero friends over for Thanksgiving dinner, but this angered Alex, who called her selfish for wanting this while their mother was hurt. However, when Katie explained that she wanted the heroes who are always alone to be together on the holiday, it caused everyone to understand what family really meant.

Action Comics #673 (1991) by Roger Stern and Bob McLeod had Clark Kent and Lois Lane celebrating Thanksgiving with the Lane family, only for them to find out that Jimmy Olsen is now homeless after getting fired from the Daily Planet, and he is on the streets away from his friends on this holiday. Superman heads out to find Jimmy, only to end up in a giant battle with "Ugly" Mannheim, the former Intergang leader, who breaks out of jail, arms himself with a rock-like suit and a nuclear device, and plans to destroy Metropolis.

Superman has to fight and defeat Mannheim before his plans can take form, and he never does find where Jimmy Olsen is. The issue does show that Jimmy finds some other people to celebrate with, as he joins Bibbo Bibbowski for a Thanksgiving party at the Ace O' Clubs, a bar that Bibbo had bought to help people living in the Suicide Slum. It was a touching story, and while Superman couldn't find Jimmy, at least the young man had someone to help take him in.

Spider-Gwen #14 (2016) by Jason Latour and Robbi Rodriguez was a Thanksgiving story that touched on both the holiday and the idea of family during this time of the year. The story was titled "Cold Turkey," and it had Gwen in a tough spot, as her father, George Stacy, was in jail, and she ended up having to make a deal with Earth-65's crime lord, Matt Murdock, who agreed to get her father freed for her. The cover teased what Matt was going to bring to Thanksgiving dinner.

This issue was also a touching one, as Gwen came across Aunt May on the commuter train, and the two had a tough talk about Peter's death (he was the Lizard in this world, but only Gwen knew the truth when he died) and how it was affecting Uncle Ben. Spider-Gwen almost got her Thanksgiving dinner with Jessica Drew and her family, but things got cut short when the Koala Kommander attacked the Thanksgiving Day parade, and she had to save the day.

Daredevil #178 (1981) by Frank Miller and Klaus Janson was a Thanksgiving superhero battle that involved several heroes, first fighting each other and then battling the real villains, all during the Thanksgiving Day parade. This was before Daredevil was friends and allies with Luke Cage and Iron Fist. Foggy Nelson hires Heroes for Hire as bodyguards for Matt Murdock while Nelson and Murdock try to tie mayoral candidate Randolph Cherryh to the Kingpin.

When Matt disappears and goes after a villain, Cage and Iron Fist think Daredevil has done something with Matt and attack him. After they fight for a bit, they finally realize they are not enemies, and they finally catch a young man named Sheldon, a blackmailer. Villains in the issue also included Kingpin, Turk, and Grotto, while Elektra meets with the Kingpin about a job in his organization, setting up her turn as his assassin, a huge turning point in the series.

One of the most iconic Thanksgiving superhero stories of all time came in the Batman comic book series Batman: The Long Halloween . This was issue #2 by Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale, and it followed the Holiday killer, whose gimmick was killing people on specific holidays. In this case, Mickey "The Mink" Sullivan's Irish crew confesses to bombing Harvey Dent and his wife, Gilda, but refuses to give up The Roman. They post bail, and when they leave, the Holiday Killer murders them all.

However, the best part of this issue came when Batman went into the sewers to find the criminals, and he ended up fighting Solomon Grundy, something he really didn't want to do. The end of the issue had a wonderful moment when a remorseful Batman returned to the sewers to leave Grundy a plate of food, allowing the monstrous man to enjoy a Thanksgiving dinner. This same scene was used in the two-part Batman animated film as well.

What are your favorite Thanksgiving comic book moments? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Dragon Ball's Official Canon is Missing Out on One of Dragon Ball GT's Best Ideas
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation One of the most tragic races in the Dragon Ball universe continues to get content made about them, but only in mostly non-canon timelines, which feels like a further twist of the knife. The Tuffles deserved much more dignified storytelling because their planet was taken from them by the Saiyans. Their peaceful race mostly focused […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the most tragic races in the Dragon Ball universe continues to get content made about them, but only in mostly non-canon timelines , which feels like a further twist of the knife. The Tuffles deserved much more dignified storytelling because their planet was taken from them by the Saiyans. Their peaceful race mostly focused on technological advances, and didn't go out searching for conflict. It came to their front door when King Vegeta led the Saiyans in a war to takeover the planet.

The Tuffles are canon in terms of the Dragon Ball Z anime, but by manga standards they are not. Akira Toriyama reportedly created them for the anime franchise , so it's a half-and-half canon argument. Explaining how the Saiyans took over Planet Vegeta, this also continued one of the enduring plot points of the Dragon Ball universe that Goku, Vegeta and the rest of the Z Fighters regularly have to clean up after their evil forefathers. The rooting interest isn't simply the Saiyans are good and their enemies are evil. Sometimes context is needed for the full story.

The reason the Tuffles are a difficult topic is that their largest amount of screen time took place in non-canon releases Dragon Ball GT featured the Tuffles more than any other prior release thanks to the invention of Baby. The evil parasite wanted to eradicate the Saiyans and bring about the resurgence of the Tuffles. As the most iconic villain of the Dragon Ball GT series overall, it made the fanbase zero-in on the Tuffles' lore and history.

Dragon Ball GT was eventually confirmed to not be a part of the official canon, so it sparked even more mystery around where the Tuffles could fall in the Dragon Ball story. The race is mentioned in Dragon Ball Super as it's revealed that the Saiyans are still living in harmony with the Tuffles in Universe 6, but their main universe story needs to come back into the canon to further expand their journey. Fans can't wipe their memory of the Baby arc, and that's the most extensive story in their history. The only logical route forward is to feature them in the Dragon Ball Super manga's future.

One of the fun parts of Dragon Ball 's multiverse is that it provides a fresh start for many arcs. The savagery the Saiyans showed in their war with the Tuffles can't be undone, but the Z Fighters can visit Universe 6 and learn about the race. It may even provide a way in for them to take Baby's now non-existent mission. Even though the Saiyans from Universe 6 are allies to Universe 7, the Tuffles might see them as bullies that eliminated their brethren. Or a group of the Tuffles might decide to wage war on the Z Fighters.

Imagine what it would then be like if Vegeta had to come to grips with his father's atrocities while simultaneously defending the innocence of the current Saiyans through this new level of context? There are numerous forks in the road that could work for this story, but it's got to get reintroduced with the Tuffles first. Do you think the Tuffles should return to the Dragon Ball story canon in the future? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: The Most Underrated Comic Book Movie of 2005 Almost Changed Hollywood, But What Happened?
articles.summary: Hollywood has always been quick to follow a visual trend. You can always expect several studios to emulate the look or approach of a film with a unique style or revisit a familiar story in an innovative way. Sometimes it's a hit, other times you get another dozen attempts to recreate the same action spectacle, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Hollywood has always been quick to follow a visual trend. You can always expect several studios to emulate the look or approach of a film with a unique style or revisit a familiar story in an innovative way. Sometimes it's a hit, other times you get another dozen attempts to recreate the same action spectacle, and still others you never really hear from again. That's one of the reasons I'm still so fascinated by this particular comic book movie from 2005. It looked like a comic book and made me ask why more filmmakers weren't doing this.

When I saw this film for the first time, I was really just amazed at what I was seeing. The cinematography, the striking black-and-white footage, and, at the end, those sudden splashes of blood red were something that was really unique in Hollywood filmmaking at the time. It wasn't just another comic book film . It was a version of a comic book movie that was pretty much a comic book. Some films later adopted the stylistic idea, but I think Hollywood missed the opportunity to push it even further.

I'm talking about Sin City , the 2005 adaptation of Miller's noir-inspired crime comics. Sin City was directed by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller , with Quentin Tarantino slipping into the director's chair for one segment. The cast featured Bruce Willis, Mickey Rourke, Clive Owen, Jessica Alba, and the rest of an equally impressive ensemble tracking down crooks, crooked cops, and doomed dames in the streets of Basin City. But Sin City wasn't merely set on a city grid that looked straight out of the '40s—it was also visualized, shot, and projected in the style of a serial comic book, with black-and-white illustrations and pop-art splashes of color complementing the breathtaking visuals.

When I first saw it, I honestly remember thinking that we had finally discovered how to make a comic book movie look like a comic book! Those flashes of red were particularly impressive. Not to mention that it looked so completely hypnotic. And the thing is, they didn't just lift the characters and basic plots; they managed to recreate the panels and compositions with insane levels of fidelity. Sin City , in my opinion, has to be one of the most faithful adaptations of a graphic novel the big screen has ever seen; it was one of the few times I wished more filmmakers would realize that visual storytelling can be just as important as the story itself.

Here's what I still find interesting. You would think, following the success of Sin City , Hollywood would have gone whole hog in adopting this unique visual style and, you know, done more graphic novel adaptations that were faithful to the look and feel of their printed counterparts. We did get Zack Snyder's 300 back in 2006, which definitely played around with some of this very unique and particular comic book style, but it hasn't really been mimicked or followed up on in the industry. Sure, many superhero movies have emulated this type of visual style with some elements of great cinematography, but very few have committed to the style that made Sin City so great.

And this is where I think streaming might finally give this idea the love it deserves. Just think about an eight-episode Sin City series that keeps a steady pace, taking in the whole of Basin City and its inhabitants. Each episode could focus on a different comic book story arc, complete with that striking black-and-white cinematography and those occasional bits of orange and yellow that contrast everything else. You could populate each episode with a new cast of actors and introduce a larger-than-life character, without losing that visual panache that makes Sin City the series that it is. Honestly, I'd be glued to my television set. Streaming services can spend a lot of money trying to create the next distinctive series, but they could find the blueprint on the pages of a comic. Give me eight episodes of glittering noir, comic-book visuals, and overly sharp characters. Seems reasonable, right?

articles.title: I Just Found Out Hallmark’s Mistletoe Murders Got A Huge Assist Thanks To … Reacher
articles.summary: I love everything about this.
articles.content:
One thing I think that’s really underrated about Hallmark is how the network’s projects manage to do a lot without the world’s largest budgets . (These aren't upcoming MCU movies !) Sometimes, however, a little bit of good karma wafts a production’s way just like a snowflake in the crisp winter air. This is exactly what happened on the set of Mistletoe Murders when the show found Fletcher’s Grove, the cool small town hide out Emily Lane ( Sarah Drew ) opens her Christmas shop in. Apparently, the show has Reacher to thank for this.

While Reacher is not known for having the insane budgets some of Amazon Prime Videos other shows like Lord of the Rings : The Rings of Power have had, the show did once create an entire facade for a small town and then left it behind after less than a month.

To Amazon’s credit, there’s a little more to it than just having an excess of money to build a whole city and dump it. Season 1 of Reacher was originally expected to film in Georgia. Then, the pandemic hit and plans changed. It was easier and safer to build a little town on a spot in the middle of nowhere in Canada, and that’s exactly what the show did.

I love it when two shows I deeply enjoy have synergy like this. Prior to being able to visit the set of Mistletoe Murders ahead of this fall's Season 3 return on the 2026 TV schedule , I would never have known the Sarah Drew-led series would have anything in common with the Alan Ritchson series, but this is one very cool connection.

articles.title: New The Batman Part 2 Set Video Teases a Major Funeral Scene, But Which One?
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. A new The Batman: Part II set video confirms a funeral is happening, but it only brings up more questions. Production on The Batman: Part II has resumed after Steven Soderbergh offered to step in to help finish the highly anticipated DC sequel, with filming on the project set to wrap in a few weeks […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new The Batman: Part II set video confirms a funeral is happening, but it only brings up more questions . Production on The Batman: Part II has resumed after Steven Soderbergh offered to step in to help finish the highly anticipated DC sequel , with filming on the project set to wrap in a few weeks after Matt Reeves was forced to step away from the project. In the time since the director change was made, details about the film have started to surface , including the identity of two key actors who joined the cast and even the presence of another Batman villain. Now DC fans have another mystery.

A new video has made its way online of production on The Batman: Part II that reveals the filming of a funeral scene, which begs the question: Who died? Obviously death in a superhero movie is kind of a given, but if the film is going out of its way to show it on screen, then they must be pretty important. This has lead to speculation that the funeral could be for the likes of Andy Serkis' Alfred, perhaps Colin Farrell's Oswald Cobblepott, or even Robert Pattinson's Bruce Wayne. Fans are also theorizing the potential that this is a flashback, maybe to the funeral of Thomas and Martha Wayne, or another character.

View this post on Instagram The Batman: Part II Funeral Scene Revealed Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. Fans immediately assuming that a funeral scene in The Batman: Part II is a sure sign that major character bites the dust in the sequel should recall that the first film had a big funeral scene for one character that was only alive on screen for maybe one full minute. The film opened with the death of Gotham City mayor Don Mitchell Jr., leading to a tense moment where another bomb-strapped victim of The Riddler literally crashed the event.

That said, it would appear that the funeral scene filmed this week for the sequel was a little less eventful, as no stunt work was caught in the set video. Plus, Serkis' Alfred was nearly killed in the last movie, they wouldn't play that card again, would they?

The gap in time between The Batman and the upcoming The Batman: Part II has only gotten bigger over the years, with the sequel's planned February 2028 release date meaning it will have been seven years between films. Some of this is due to simply delays in production, but now fans are beginning to wonder about what the future holds for the series thanks to two of the biggest stories out of Hollywood this year.

First up is that DC Studios has undergone a massive leadership change , with James Gunn and Peter Safran being replaced by Jeremy Latcham. Though the new boss won't officially be in charge until December 1st, it has many wondering how he will handle his duties after being handpicked by the Skydance brass, with many assuming that it means The Batman series will come to an end as they brace for their own take on the DC superhero.

The second big change, of course, is that Robert Pattinson has already secured his next major role, being cast as the new James Bond for Amazon MGM Studios new film in the series. Reports have already begun to circulate that Pattinson may have been released from his initial deal with DC, which called for him to appear in three Batman movies, with the delays in the sequel putting an end to it. With another major franchises under his belt as 007, fans believe there's no way Pattinson can juggle both.

All of that is to say that these two stories are why some fans believe that the funeral scene being shot for The Batman: Part II is actually for Pattinson's Bruce Wayne himself. The end of the road appears to be approaching for the series, and putting a firm end on it doesn't seem out of the question. That in mind, would a massive spoiler like this actually be shot out in public? Time will tell, but we still have over a year before the movie is released.

Whose funeral do you think was being filmed for The Batman: Part II? Sound off with your best theory in the comments below.

articles.title: Is Deadpool 4 Happening? Ryan Reynolds' Marvel Future Teased in New Report
articles.summary: Marvel Studios There are so many questions swirling around Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars, as the two game-changing films will clear out the cluttered past of Marvel movies and relaunch the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a complete collection of characters, in which The Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men, and Spider-Man will all be playing in the same […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are so many questions swirling around Avengers : Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars , as the two game-changing films will clear out the cluttered past of Marvel movies and relaunch the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a complete collection of characters, in which The Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men, and Spider-Man will all be playing in the same cinematic sandbox for the very first time.

Not every character we know and love from Marvel movies will make it to the new era of the MCU, though. But while some legacy characters can easily be recast (or already have been), others are so connected to the actors playing them that it's almost impossible to imagine them being played by anyone else. And Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool is definitely one of the characters.

So what's happening with Deadpool after Avengers: Doomsday and Secret Wars ? We may be getting our first real indication of that answer.

Ryan Reynolds is making headlines in Hollywood after signing with a new publicist (Kelly Bush Novak), who also represents his wife, actress Blake Lively. THR did a profile on Reynolds, and in it, the trade notes that the actor "has another Deadpool movie coming after the box office success of 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine."

A lot of fans and outlets take that sentence to mean Ryan Reynolds is coming back for another Deadpool movie (which would technically be Deadpool 4 ); however, that is not quite accurate. For those keeping track: it's been indicated that while Ryan Reynolds may still play Deadpool in Phase Seven of the MCU, he won't necessarily be continuing his solo film franchise.

When asked last year if he's had any talks with Reynolds about the future of Deadpool in the MCU, Kevin Feige confirmed that they have been talking about it. “There have absolutely been discussions. We’re in touch with Ryan a lot. So the answer is yes.”

Around that same time, Ryan Reynolds confirmed that he is already working on this next Deadpool film, and that it isn't a solo film: “I’m writing something right now… It’s a little ensemble." Reynolds said.

It makes sense that Marvel Studios would make a clean break from the Fox X-Men Universe, where Deadpool and Deadpool 2 took place, and not continue the solo film franchise. At the same time, Ryan Reynolds is so deeply tied to Deadpool (and beloved as the character) that recasting would be a nightmare. It's a conundrum that can be easily solved, though. There is a precedent in Marvel Comics of Deadpool being someone who is uniquely aware of changes to reality or the timeline, due to his fourth-wall awareness. So Deadpool tends to remain a constant, even when everything else in reality shifts.

The MCU can have a lot of fun with that concept, but admittedly, it'll be a dynamic that works far better when Deadpool is onscreen with groups of other characters who are completely unaware that Phase Seven is a reboot, with a whole new version of the X-Men. It's also one of the only ways Marvel will still be able to induge in some nostalgia, while still establishing the new version of the franchise.

Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th. Deadpool & Wolverine is streaming on Disney+.

articles.title: 5 Starfleet Starships That Can Survive Just About Any Fight
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Skydance Star Trek has been successful over the years for a variety of reasons. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Trek has been successful over the years for a variety of reasons. It was hopeful sci-fi during a time of great upheaval, connecting to a fanbase that kept the show alive even when it wasn't on TV. The franchise showed us a future where everyone could work together and have any kind of life they want, all in the pursuit of science and exploration. Fans fell in love with the characters of the various shows, but there's a section of the fanbase who loved a different kind of Star Trek character – the ships. I have been a proud ship geek since I was a child and I'm not alone; there are dozens of us (Dozens!).

Each race in Star Trek has their own ship design philosophy. The Klingons and the Romulans like war, so their ships are often warships. The Federation's Starfleet is first and foremost about exploration and diplomacy, but they aren't stupid. They know it's a dangerous galaxy and so they arm their ships quite well. They even began to build more warships as the years went on, especially the Battle of Wolf-359 and the Dominion War. These five Starfleet ships are the toughest in the fleet and have brought their crews home when others wouldn't.

Star Trek: The Next Generation perfectly rebooted Trek , introducing fans to the newest Starfleet vessel – the Galaxy -class. 641 meters long, with a beam of 473 meters and a height of 133 meters, it was the largest vessel in the fleet at the time of launch. It was a basically a flying Federation embassy, equipped with the latest in technology. It was well-armed for a Starfleet vessel, with 12 phasers strips and fore and aft torpedo launchers; it could use its phasers to destroy a planet by boring to the core. It was state of the art, but unfortunately that doesn't mean invincible.

Galaxy -class ships had their weaknesses and we saw plenty get destroyed over the years. They weren't made for combat (I mean, so much of the surface area is literally just viewport instead of armor), so when the Dominion War started, these giant ships were getting taken down left and right, the smaller, faster Jem'Hadar fighters cutting through them. Starfleet couldn't let this stand, so as the war went on, they made the ships even more powerful, souping up the armor and weapons. A few Dominion War Galaxies could stand off with the biggest ships in the Dominion, forming a powerful bulwark on the firing line, or wade into the fray and destroy smaller ships without even trying. The modifications made to the class would be incorporated into the Ross -class down the line.

The Constitution -class is one of the most important hulls in Starfleet history. First launched in the 2240s, there have been three different versions of the ship, with the Constitution III- class (or the Neo-Connie, as I've heard her referred to as) still in service in the 25th century. Connies made up the backbone of the fleet until the Excelsior -class came along in the later years of 23rd century, earning its reputation as one of the most versatile ships of all time. They were first built when tensions with the Klingons were at their highest, so they were meant to take a beating and give one.

A Connie had six dual phasers turrets on its saucer section, with a forward-firing torpedo launcher. Refit Connies and Neos had dual fore launchers and an aft launcher. Neos had more phasers banks as well, with seven phaser turrets and four phaser arrays. While none of them were going to be confused for gunships, their weapons were quite powerful, as fits the best ship in the fleet during their time. It was also one of the toughest ships ever built, able to withstand brutal weapons' barrages ( Wrath of Khan for the refit or the Neo's battle with the Shrike in Picard Season Three) and keep fighting. Connies kept the Federation free for decades and became legendary.

Star Trek has some terrifying villains , but none of them can match the Borg. The cybernetic race wants to assimilate the entire galaxy into the Borg Collective and their ships are some of the most powerful ever. Starfleet learned this at the Battle of Wolf 359, where one Borg Cube destroyed 39 ships, killing thousands on its way to Earth. Starfleet panicked and began to design ships that were warships first, something that they didn't do against the Klingons or Romulans. This led to numerous new classes of ship, including the Akira -class.

The Akira -class has two design elements that make it a perfect warship – its torpedo pod and its launch bays. The Akira 's torpedo pod is armed 9 or 10 launchers, four forward, three starboard aft and three port aft, with at least two quantum torpedo launchers in the fore batteries. They set on a rotary system, allowing rapid torpedo fire. The saucer also has several more launchers, including port and starboard ones, allowing them to fire torpedo broadsides. The ship has a "fly-through" launch bay, with launch doors in the front and back of the ship. Also armed with numerous phaser arrays, the Akira is able to do massive amounts of damage with its torpedoes, as well as field numerous smaller craft.

The Sovereign -class was launched in the early 2370s and was meant to replace the Galaxy as the flagship. It was smaller by volume, but it was longer, at 685 meters long, with a beam of 249 meters and a length of 88 meters. It was also substantially better armed and armored, the lessons of Wolf-359 making it a formidable warship. It was armed with 12 phaser arrays, a quantum torpedo launcher, 2 forward torpedo launchers, and three aft. The class was refitted before 2379, which added four more phasers arrays, another forward torpedo launcher and three more in the aft.

The Sovereign was an example of Starfleet learning the lesson of the Galaxy -class. Galaxy -class ships were powerful, but they were not warships. The Sovereign joined the lineage of the Enterprise , with the NCC-1701-E a Sovereign . The Sovereign has all of the scientific equipment of a Galaxy , it's just tougher, faster, and better armed. It was the total package, able to both catalog spatial anomalies and take down an entire fleet of enemy vessels on it own.

The Defiant -class was the first ship created to deal with the Borg. Lieutenant Commander Benjamin Sisko, one of the survivors of Wolf-359, helped design the ship. Unlike some of the post-Wolf-359 designs, the Defiant -class was created completely to be a gunship. Its main armaments were four forward pulse phaser cannons on the nacelles, two forward quantum torpedo launchers, two forward photon torpedo launchers and two aft, and three phasers arrays. The nose contained both the navigational deflector and a phaser array, and could be launched as a missile. The ship's deflectors were amazingly powerful and the hull was equipped with ablative armor, making it an extremely tough egg to crack. As far as other systems, if it wasn't combat-focused, it was underpowered or even non-existent.

The prototype's warp core was vastly overpowered to handle all of that, with several shakedown cruises making that name literal. With the Dominion threat intensifying, the Defiant NX-74205 was assigned to DS9, equipped with a Romulan cloaking device for recon missions. The Defiant -class was classified as an "escort vessel", meant to work with other ships in wolf pack tactics, overwhelming larger targets. They were fast and maneuverable, able to get in quick to bigger vessels and pound them with fire. They were amazing in combat and one of the coolest starships in Star Trek history.

What Starfleet ships do you think are the toughest? Which ones would take into battle? How weak is an Oberth really? Sound off in the comment section below.

Still, with wind levels of up to 23 mph - and gusts considerably stronger - the postponement appears to have been justified, and the worst of the storm is yet to come.

The impact of the postponement on performances that had been scheduled for today - marching bands, celebrity appearances, the big Broadway medley involving nine different shows - was still be dealt with as of this morning. While Coss didn't specify which performances are on schedule, Deadline can confirm that the Broadway medley that was planned in lieu of the traditional individual show performances is a go for Saturday. The Book of Mormon had a simple message on its IG page about the date switch: "Ready and psyched."

As for other non-Broadway performers originally scheduled for Thursday, reports are filtering in piecemeal on whether they'll make the move to Saturday. The New York Post has reported that Smash Mouth will perform, and Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete are expected as well, as are the Radio City Rockettes. Billy Evans , Elizabeth Holmes ’ partner and the father of their two children, took to X on Nov. 26 to write an emotional Thanksgiving message to her.

The text is primarily about how much he misses her and how their kids need their mother. Holmes is currently serving an 11-year prison sentence for four wire fraud-related convictions tied to her high-tech health company, Theranos.

“Today is our fourth Thanksgiving with Liz in prison,” Evans wrote. “Despite everything, I have so much to be thankful for. articles.title: MCU Fantastic Four Reboot Lost Disney Money Despite $500 Million Box Office
articles.summary: If you don’t count Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Doomsday, The Fantastic Four: First Steps was easily one of the most anticipated movies from Marvel Studios since Endgame. The film brought Marvel’s First Family into the MCU and laid the groundwork for Doomsday and seemed like it was off to an impressive start when […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you don’t count Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Doomsday, The Fantastic Four: First Steps was easily one of the most anticipated movies from Marvel Studios since Endgame. The film brought Marvel’s First Family into the MCU and laid the groundwork for Doomsday and seemed like it was off to an impressive start when it hit theaters in July 2025. However, it turns out that the film may have made half a billion at the box office and still ended up losing money.

According to Forbes , The Fantastic Four: First Steps “exceeded the production budget” and ended up costing $371.1 million to make. When all of the accounting was said and done, including a $73.5 million reimbursement that reduced the film’s net spending to $297.6 million, once you account for the 50/50 split in box office earnings on the film’s $521.9 million earnings, the film came up $36.7 million short.

There’s actually a good bit about the revelation regarding The Fantastic Four: First Steps and its profitability that is interesting. The biggest might just be that this is a rare glimpse at the actual numbers behind the scenes. Generally speaking, we don’t get these specific disclosures — these sort of details aren’t the kind of things that get disclosed in the United States. However, the rules are a bit different in the U.K. Films made in the U.K. can benefit from specific credits and reimbursement based on percentage of production costs incurred in the U .K. which means the details have to be filed — and that’s where the numbers come from.

But beyond the very specific nerdiness of the money of it all, The Fantastic Four: First Steps is certainly not the only MCU film believed to have lost money. The Marvels , Thunderbolts* , Captain America: Brave New World , and The Incredible Hulk are all regularly cited as having lost money at the box office. It’s possible that Eternals is also among that list, though that’s somewhat disputed as the estimates are pretty tight. If you look at the movies that fall into the “poor box office” category here, however, there’s a bit of a pattern. These are movies that are more directly setting up themes, structure, and in some cases even characters that are necessary for future storytelling. I think that it’s worth considering that for many MCU fans, Marvel movies are largely defined by “big” characters they are already very familiar with. When you start bringing in other stories, those movies perform a little less well — but they’re just as important to the larger picture and the bigger story being told.

That in particular is something that we should see play out specifically when Avengers: Endgame hits theaters next month. After all, everything we’ve seen so far makes it pretty clear that the Fantastic Four play a significant part — and it’s already looking very good for that film’s box office.

Are you surprised about this detail about The Fantastic Four: First Steps’ box office? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: I Love The Emperor's New Groove, But David Spade Has Some Blunt Thoughts About Disney
articles.summary: You threw off my groove!
articles.content:
The Emperor’s New Groove is one of those Walt Disney Animation movies that will forever and always be imprinted in my brain. The 2000 film came out at just the right time in my childhood when I’d put it on repeat. I could honestly quote most of it front to back. However, I had no idea about the experience Kuzco's voice actor, David Spade , had.

Hey, he makes a good point. Prior to the 21st Century, animated movies weren't paying big-name celebrities the big bucks. David Spade was also working with Disney Animation at a time when the studio wasn’t making blockbusters to the degree it is now with the likes of Frozen or Moana . Spade even disclosed how much he made, saying this:

Shrek came out in 2001 – one year after The Emperor’s New Groove – and made almost half a billion worldwide. It helped usher in an era of blockbuster animated films led by A-list celebrities that we continue to live in. The Emperor's New Groove made $169 million worldwide, and was actually thought of as a commercial flop at the time of its release.

Animated movies like The Emperor’s New Groove famously go through a long production process. The 2000 movie in particular did so because it was actually originally an entirely different movie called Kingdom of the Sun . It was more inspired by The Prince and the Pauper , featured Owen Wilson in a voice role, and Spade was playing a character named Manco instead of Kuzco before they shifted directions. No wonder he was getting antsy while making it!

Forced to contend with the dual problems of a telepath who body hops from person to person, and strange changes to his abilities, he forms a partnership with the Punisher . SFX ’s reviewer said it "remains true to the previous Holland-led films in that it’s character-driven, emotional, comical and grounded. But it’s also something more, giving us what we expect yet also delivering on darker, more mature themes as the web-slinger ages up and faces fresh challenges”. Spider-Man: Brand New Day is out to buy on DVD, Blu-ray™ and 4K UHD from 14 December. Extras-wise, you get 10 featurettes (totalling about 69 minutes) plus a three-minute gag reel. We have five Blu-rays to give away. To put your name in the hat for the chance to win one, simply answer the question below.
